title: Hours added to drivers' commutes after flash floods overwhelm New York State Thruway - NewsBreak
text: ROCHESTER, N.Y. (WROC) — Heavy rainfall and flash floods across the Rochester area on Wednesday afternoon presented challenges for many folks on the roads and in their homes. Downpours first struck Rochester mid-afternoon Wednesday, although many towns south of the Thruway experienced them beforehand. Aman Syed, who is originally from San Jose, C.A., stopped at the Seneca Rest Stop in Victor on his way to Niagara Falls Wednesday evening. After traveling most of the day, he expressed his frustration with the inclement weather conditions . “There have been a lot of crashes on the road and a lot of traffic. It was raining the entire time, zero visibility, and the roads were absolutely wet and nasty,” Syed said. Past the Seneca Rest Stop, near westbound Exit 46 on the thruway, many motorists witnessed the effects of Wednesday’s flash flooding firsthand as a stretch of road was submerged in water. According to New York State Police, this resulted in temporary lane closures in both directions. Barbara & Matthew Metz from Farmington had to drive through the rain to pick their son up from work and were shocked by the extent of the flooding. “I wasn’t expecting it to be downpouring when I left,” Barbara said. “It’s hard for me to see when driving when it downpours.” Many folks who live in the Rochester area reported flooding in their basements and backyards as a result of the torrential downpours. Sarah VanVector, a thruway traveler who was driving home to Indiana from Vermont Wednesday evening, explained the difficult conditions she was faced with bearing the storms. “I was rerouted two hours out of the way, which I didn’t want to do,” VanVector said. “Seeing the delay was frustrating, especially because I just want to go back home.” New York State Police confirmed no injuries or accidents resulted from the excess flooding on the Thruway near Exit 46 and crews are working to clear the excess water from the roadway.
